call_points.text: No volume or margin guidance for FY27; management said the situation is too fluid to hazard a guess.
Q1FY27 margin was an aberration: GPPS delta rose from USD200 to 300-plus, HIPS from USD275-300 to 400-plus.
Non-OEM demand fell almost 50% in Q1FY27 but has started returning as customers accept higher prices.
Total capex across all expansions is about ₹900 Cr, funded entirely from internal accruals.
Terminal ABS capacity after full expansion will be 1,40,000 tpa nameplate.
All expansions will be funded from internal accruals, with no external debt mentioned.
EPS Phase-II expansion at Nagothane was successfully commissioned on April 14, 2026, enhancing capacity to 115,000 tons per annum.
Non-OEM segment demand took a big beating in April due to high prices, labor unavailability, and gas shortages.
The company remains debt-free with an investable surplus of ₹700 crores as of March 2026.
Styrene monomer prices rose sharply in March 2026 to a peak of around $1,650 per ton following the West Asia conflict.

operating_notes.text: EPS Phase-II expansion at Nagothane commissioned on April 14, 2026, increasing EPS capacity to 115,000 tons per annum.
Q1FY27 sales volume of manufactured products was 70,842 MT versus 93,853 MT a year ago, a 24.5% decline.
Styrene monomer landed CIF price in India is around USD1,300, with Q1FY27 range USD1,350-1,400 and a peak above USD1,500.
About 20,000 tonnes of polystyrene was imported in Q1FY27, in line with the roughly 87,000 tonnes annual imports last year.
